title: Site comparison respects the normalized open base-change map
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring, and let
$$\begin{array}{ccc}U'&\xrightarrow h&U\\
j'\downarrow&&\downarrow j\\
X'&\xrightarrow g&X\end{array}$$
be an open-immersion square of schemes [def-cbc-open-immersion-square], with arbitrary $g$. Use the bounded-below ordinary constant-$\Lambda$ module derived categories on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and ordinary unbounded constant-$\Lambda$ module derived categories on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $N_T=\nu_T^*$ for the exact derived site comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and let
$\rho_u:u_{\mathrm{proet}}^{-1}N_V\xrightarrow{\sim}N_Tu_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}$ be the inverse of the canonical comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. Use exact open extensions on both sites [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact, lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. Let $c_j:N_Xj_!^{\mathrm{et}}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!^{\mathrm{proet}}N_U$ be the degreewise extension to derived categories of the specified sheaf comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. Its inverse is the $j_!^{\mathrm{proet}}\dashv j_{\mathrm{proet}}^{-1}$ adjunct of
$$N_UK\xrightarrow{N_U\eta^{\mathrm{et}}_{j,K}}N_Uj_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}j_!^{\mathrm{et}}K\xrightarrow{\rho_{j,j_!^{\mathrm{et}}K}^{-1}}j_{\mathrm{proet}}^{-1}N_Xj_!^{\mathrm{et}}K,$$
where $\eta_j^{\mathrm{et}}$ is the etale open-adjunction unit. Define $c_{j'}$ similarly. Let $e_j^{\mathrm{et}}:g_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}j_!^{\mathrm{et}}\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!{}^{\mathrm{et}}h_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}$ and $e_j^{\mathrm{proet}}:g_{\mathrm{proet}}^{-1}j_!^{\mathrm{proet}}\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!{}^{\mathrm{proet}}h_{\mathrm{proet}}^{-1}$ be the actual comparisons of [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change, lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change]. Then for every $K\in D^+(U_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$,
$$j'_!{}^{\mathrm{proet}}(\rho_{h,K})\circ e_{j,N_UK}^{\mathrm{proet}}\circ g_{\mathrm{proet}}^{-1}(c_{j,K})
=c_{j',h_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}K}\circ N_{X'}(e_{j,K}^{\mathrm{et}})\circ\rho_{g,j_!^{\mathrm{et}}K}.$$
Both sides are morphisms from $g_{\mathrm{proet}}^{-1}N_Xj_!^{\mathrm{et}}K$ to $j'_!{}^{\mathrm{proet}}N_{U'}h_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}K$ in $D(X'_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$. The normalization and equality are natural in $K$.

proof.text: The sheaf comparison of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] is natural in the etale sheaf and compatible with composition of open immersions. Since extension by zero is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], its componentwise comparison gives the stated natural isomorphism c_j on bounded-below derived objects; the same applies to j′. The inverse-image comparison rho_u is the canonical comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], so its orientation is the inverse of the comparison displayed there and is compatible with the cartesian square.

source.place: Tag 09AF, lemma-jshriek-comparison; Tag 099R, comparison inverse image

proof.text: Reduction to sheaves and the two inverse-unit formulas. For $K\in D^+(U_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ every arrow in the displayed equation is the image in $D(X'_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ of a degreewise map of complexes: $c_j,c_{j'}$ by definition (step 1), $\rho_g,\rho_h$ because the comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] is a natural isomorphism of exact functors applied termwise, $e^{\mathrm{et}}_j$ because [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change] states that it is its canonical sheaf-level map applied degreewise to the complex, and $e^{\mathrm{proet}}_j$ because [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change] is stated for complexes; all functors $N$, $u^{-1}$, $j_!$ are exact and act degreewise ([lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]). Hence it suffices to prove the equality for a single etale $\Lambda$-module sheaf $F$ on $U$ in each degree, using the underived adjunctions $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$, $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$. For such $F$: (i) by [lem-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change-underived-compatibility], $(e^{\mathrm{et}}_{j,F})^{-1}$ is the $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$ transpose of $s_g\circ h^{-1}(\eta^{\mathrm{et}}_{j,F}):h^{-1}F\to j'^{-1}g^{-1}j_!F$, where $s_g:h^{-1}j^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}j'^{-1}g^{-1}$ is the cartesian inverse-image identification; (ii) by [lem-cbc-finite-open-exchange-scalars] with $B=C=\Lambda$, $a=\mathrm{id}$, for every pro-etale module sheaf $M$ on $U$ the map $(e^{\mathrm{proet}}_{j,M})^{-1}$ is the transpose of $\sigma_{j_!M}\circ h^{-1}(\eta^{\mathrm{proet}}_{j,M})$, with $\sigma:h^{-1}j^{-1}\cong j'^{-1}g^{-1}$ the site-composition comparison named in that statement.

source.place: Tag 03S6, lemma-shriek-base-change (restriction of $j'_!f'^{-1}$ and $f^{-1}j_!$ to $U'$ identified by the units)

proof.text: Unit formula for the site comparison of extensions. Write $a_u=\rho_u^{-1}:N_Tu^{-1}_{\mathrm{et}}\to u^{-1}_{\mathrm{proet}}N_V$, the canonical comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. The unit-normalization theorem [lem-sf-open-comparison-unit-normalization], whose $c$ is the comparison of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] and whose $a$ is this canonical $a_j$, gives $j^{-1}(c_{j,F})\circ a_{j,j_!F}\circ N_U(\eta^{\mathrm{et}}_{j,F})=\eta^{\mathrm{proet}}_{j,N_UF}$. Applying $j^{-1}(c_{j,F}^{-1})$, the transpose of $c_{j,F}^{-1}$, namely $j^{-1}(c_{j,F}^{-1})\circ\eta^{\mathrm{proet}}_{j,N_UF}$, equals $a_{j,j_!F}\circ N_U(\eta^{\mathrm{et}}_{j,F})=\rho_{j,j_!F}^{-1}\circ N_U(\eta^{\mathrm{et}}_{j,F})$. This proves the normalization of $c_j^{-1}$ asserted in the statement, and likewise for $c_{j'}$.

Transposes of the two inverses. Both sides of the displayed equation are isomorphisms, so it suffices to show that their inverses $\Phi$ (left) and $\Psi$ (right), maps $j'_!N_{U'}h^{-1}F\to g^{-1}N_Xj_!F$, have equal transposes $P:=N_{U'}h^{-1}F\to j'^{-1}g^{-1}N_Xj_!F$ under $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$; transposition is a bijection, with $(f\circ j'_!\varphi)^\sharp=f^\sharp\circ\varphi$ and $(\psi\circ f)^\sharp=j'^{-1}(\psi)\circ f^\sharp$. Left: $\Phi=g^{-1}(c_{j,F}^{-1})\circ(e^{\mathrm{proet}}_{j,N_UF})^{-1}\circ j'_!(a_{h,F})$. By step 2(ii), naturality of $\sigma$ and step 3, $\Phi^\sharp=\sigma\circ h^{-1}\big(j^{-1}(c_{j,F}^{-1})\circ\eta^{\mathrm{proet}}_{j,N_UF}\big)\circ a_{h,F}=\sigma\circ h^{-1}(a_{j,j_!F})\circ h^{-1}N_U(\eta^{\mathrm{et}}_{j,F})\circ a_{h,F}$, and naturality of $a_h$ rewrites this as $\big[\sigma\circ h^{-1}(a_j)\circ a_h\big]_{j_!F}\circ N_{U'}h^{-1}(\eta^{\mathrm{et}}_{j,F})$. Right: $\Psi=a_{g,j_!F}\circ N_{X'}((e^{\mathrm{et}}_{j,F})^{-1})\circ c_{j',h^{-1}F}^{-1}$. By step 3 for $j'$, naturality of $a_{j'}$ and step 2(i), $\Psi^\sharp=j'^{-1}(a_g)\circ a_{j'}\circ N_{U'}\big(j'^{-1}((e^{\mathrm{et}})^{-1})\circ\eta^{\mathrm{et}}_{j'}\big)=\big[j'^{-1}(a_g)\circ a_{j'}\circ N_{U'}(s_g)\big]_{j_!F}\circ N_{U'}h^{-1}(\eta^{\mathrm{et}}_{j,F})$.

Coherence and conclusion. The two bracketed transformations $N_{U'}h^{-1}j^{-1}\to j'^{-1}g^{-1}N_X$ are the comparisons for the composite $U'\to X$ along the factorizations $j\circ h$ and $g\circ j'$, transported by the cartesian identifications $s_g$ (etale) and $\sigma$ (pro-etale) of [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. The comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] is compatible with composites and with that cartesian identification, so $\sigma\circ h^{-1}(a_j)\circ a_h=j'^{-1}(a_g)\circ a_{j'}\circ N_{U'}(s_g)$. Hence $\Phi^\sharp=\Psi^\sharp$, so $\Phi=\Psi$, and inverting gives the displayed equality degreewise, hence in $D(X'_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ by step 2. Every arrow used is natural in $F$, so the equality is natural in $K$.

proof.text: The construction also covers the identity square, an empty open, the zero complex, and the zero coefficient ring: each comparison is then the corresponding identity or zero map, and the mate calculation is unchanged. No hypothesis on g beyond the given commutative open-immersion square is used.

That formula, with the etale formula of lem-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change-underived-compatibility, proves the item by itself, so the new node is unneeded. The new node is true (V×_X X'=V×_U U') but unused, so I dropped it.
